blocks.text: Power BI is four jobs done in order. Raw files go in on the left. A report other people can use comes out on the right. Each week of this plan covers one job.
The four highlighted boxes all live inside Power BI Desktop. Most beginner trouble with DAX is really an unfinished job one or two boxes to the left.
Before day 1

items: **Install Power BI Desktop.** It is free, from the Microsoft Store or the Microsoft download page.

**You are on a Mac, and Power BI Desktop runs on Windows only.** Use a Windows virtual machine (Parallels or similar), a cloud Windows PC, or a spare Windows laptop. The Power BI website alone is not enough for weeks 1 to 3.
**No account is needed to build.** You need a work or school account only when you publish and share, which is week 8.

blocks.text: **Goal** turn a messy file into a tidy table**Time** 10 hours**You finish with** a clean Orders query that refreshes with one click
Power Query is a recorder. Every click you make to clean the data is saved as a step. When a new file arrives next month, Power BI replays the steps for you. You never edit the source file by hand.
**Query**One recipe that produces one table.*Like a saved macro, but readable.*
**Applied Steps**The list on the right. Each row is one change. You can click any step to see the data at that point, rename it, or delete it.
**Data types**Text, whole number, decimal, date. Wrong types cause wrong sums and broken date charts. Set them on purpose.
**Unpivot**Turns month columns (Jan, Feb, Mar) into rows. Charts and slicers need one column per kind of thing.
**Merge and Append**Merge adds columns from another table by a matching key. Append stacks rows of tables with the same columns.*Merge is a join. Append is a union.*
**Close & Apply**Loads the cleaned result into the model. Until you press it, the report still has the old data.
Watch the steps work
Applied Steps on the first rows of orders_raw.csv
Orange dots mark stray spaces. Step 5 leaves the missing amount as `null`. That is correct: a blank is unknown, and turning it into 0 would lower your averages.

Wide (how people type it)
Long (what Power BI wants)
Select the product column, then Transform, Unpivot Columns, Unpivot Other Columns. A new month next quarter becomes new rows, so nothing in the report breaks.

blocks.text: Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: After Changed Type, dates such as 14/01/2025 show Error while 03/01/2025 loads as 1 March. What is the right fix?
options: Replace errors with null and move on
Delete the step, then use Change Type, Using Locale, with a day-first locale such as English (India)
Keep the column as text
Open the CSV and retype the dates as month/day/year
quiz.why: Your machine reads dates month-first, so day 14 is invalid and day 3 is silently read as March. Using Locale tells Power Query the source is day-first. Replacing errors would hide wrong dates.

quiz.q: A sheet has columns Product, Jan, Feb, Mar holding sales. You want one Month slicer and one line chart. What do you do in Power Query?
options: Select Jan, Feb and Mar and Merge Columns
Transpose the table
Select Product, then Unpivot Other Columns
Add a custom column that sums the three months
quiz.why: Unpivot turns the three month columns into two columns, Month and Value. Unpivot Other Columns also picks up Apr automatically when it appears.

quiz.q: Next month a new orders file arrives in the same layout and replaces the old one. What do you have to do?
options: Repeat every cleaning step by hand
Copy the M code into a new query
Press Refresh. The applied steps run again on the new file
Clean the file in Excel first
quiz.why: Applied Steps are a recorded recipe. Refresh replays them on whatever data the source now holds.

blocks.text: **Goal** connect tables so one slicer filters everything**Time** 10 hours**You finish with** a star schema of Orders, Products, Stores and Date

A model is a set of tables joined by relationships. Instead of one giant sheet with everything repeated, you keep events in one table and descriptions in small lookup tables. Power BI then knows that choosing Tea in the Products table should filter the matching orders.
**Fact table**Things that happened. One row per order, payment or visit. Long, mostly numbers and keys.*Here: Orders.*
**Dimension table**Things you describe and filter by. One row per product, store or day. Short, mostly text.*Here: Products, Stores, Date.*
**Relationship**A line between a key column in two tables. Almost always one-to-many: one product, many orders.
**Filter direction**Filters flow from the one side to the many side. A product filter reaches orders. An order filter does not reach products.
**Date table**One row per calendar day with year, month and quarter columns. Needed for month sorting and for year-to-date measures in week 3.
**Star schema**One fact in the middle, dimensions around it. Simple to read, fast, and the shape DAX expects.
The Kettle & Crumb star schema
Pick a category in Products and the filter travels along the arrow into Orders. Nothing travels back, which is why dimensions never filter each other by accident.
Why not one flat table?

rows: Repeated on every order row. One typo creates a new category.
Grows with every repeated text value.
Small. Text lives in short tables.

blocks.text: Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: You put Products[category] and a sum of Orders[amount] in a table. Tea, Coffee and Bakery all show the same grand total. What is the most likely cause?
options: The amount column is text
There is no active relationship between Products and Orders
The visual needs a slicer
Auto date/time is switched on
quiz.why: With no relationship, a category filter cannot reach Orders, so every row shows the unfiltered total. Open Model view and connect Products[product] to Orders[product].

quiz.q: In the relationship between Products and Orders, which statement is correct?
options: Orders is the one side and filters Products
Products is the one side. A filter on Products flows to Orders
Both are many, so it must be many-to-many
Direction does not matter in a star schema
quiz.why: Each product appears once in Products and many times in Orders. Filters travel from the one side to the many side.

quiz.q: Orders has an order date column. You want to analyse by month, quarter and weekday, and later use year-to-date measures. What is the best setup?
options: Add Month and Quarter columns inside Orders
Rely on the automatic date hierarchy
Create a separate Date table with one row per day, relate it to Orders[order date], and mark it as a date table
Convert the date to text such as 2025-01
quiz.why: A dedicated Date table works for every fact table, sorts months correctly, includes days with no orders, and is what the time intelligence functions expect.

blocks.text: **Goal** write measures that stay correct under any filter**Time** 12 hours**You finish with** ten measures, from Total Sales to month-over-month growth

DAX looks like Excel formulas, but it works on whole columns and tables, never on a cell like B2. One idea explains most of it: a measure has no fixed answer. It is recalculated for every cell of every visual, using only the rows that survive the current filters. Those surviving rows are the filter context.
Filter context simulator

Click the slicers. Highlighted rows are the filter context, and every measure is computed from those rows only. The last measure uses CALCULATE to remove the region filter, so its denominator ignores your region choice.
**Measure**A formula calculated when a visual asks for it. Changes with slicers. Use for anything you total, average or divide.
**Calculated column**A formula calculated once per row at refresh and stored. Use for values you slice or group by, such as a price band.
**Row context**Working through a table one row at a time. Calculated columns and the X functions (SUMX, AVERAGEX) have it.
**CALCULATE**Runs a measure under changed filters. Add one, replace one, or remove one. It is the most used function in DAX.
**Time intelligence**Ready-made date shifts: TOTALYTD, DATEADD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR. They need the marked Date table from week 2.
**Variables**`VAR` stores a step, `RETURN` gives the result. Easier to read and to debug.
Measure or calculated column?

rows: Can go on a slicer or axis

blocks.text: Rule of thumb: if the answer is a number shown in a card, table or chart, write a measure. Reach for a column only when you need to filter or group by the result.
The ten measures to learn, in order

blocks.code:
Total Sales   = SUMX ( Orders, Orders[qty] * RELATED ( Products[price] ) )
Orders Count  = COUNTROWS ( Orders )
Avg Order     = DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], [Orders Count] )
Total Cost    = SUMX ( Orders, Orders[qty] * RELATED ( Products[unit_cost] ) )
Profit        = [Total Sales] - [Total Cost]
Margin %      = DIVIDE ( [Profit], [Total Sales] )
Tea Sales     = CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], Products[category] = "Tea" )
% of Regions  = DIVIDE ( [Total Sales],
                    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS ( Stores[region] ) ) )
Sales YTD     = TOTALYTD ( [Total Sales], 'Date'[Date] )
Sales MoM %   =
    VAR Prev = CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATEADD ( 'Date'[Date], -1, MONTH ) )
    RETURN DIVIDE ( [Total Sales] - Prev, Prev )

Mistakes beginners make this week

items: Averaging a percentage column. Divide the totals in a measure and the result is right at every level.
Using `/` where the bottom can be zero. `DIVIDE` returns blank and avoids the error.
Writing `SUM(Orders[qty]) * SUM(Products[price])`. That multiplies two totals. Use SUMX to multiply row by row.

blocks.text: Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: You need Margin % that is correct for one product, one region and the grand total. How do you build it?
options: A calculated column of profit ÷ amount per row, then average it
A measure: DIVIDE([Profit], [Total Sales])
A calculated column, then sum it
Type the percentages into a new table
quiz.why: A ratio must be recalculated from totals at each level. Averaging row percentages gives a small order the same weight as a large one.

quiz.q: A North slicer is on. A card should show North's share of sales across all regions. Which measure does that?
options: DIVIDE([Total Sales], [Total Sales])
DIVIDE([Total Sales], SUM(Orders[amount]))
DIVIDE([Total Sales], CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS(Stores[region])))
CALCULATE([Total Sales], Stores[region] = "North")
quiz.why: The top keeps the slicer. The bottom uses CALCULATE with REMOVEFILTERS to ignore the region filter. Try it in the simulator: the last measure works this way.

quiz.q: Orders has qty. Products has price. Which measure gives correct revenue?
options: SUM(Orders[qty]) * SUM(Products[price])
SUMX(Orders, Orders[qty] * RELATED(Products[price]))
SUM(Orders[qty] * Products[price])
AVERAGE(Products[price]) * COUNTROWS(Orders)
quiz.why: SUMX walks Orders row by row, RELATED fetches that row's price across the relationship, and the products are added up. Multiplying two totals mixes every quantity with every price.

blocks.text: **Goal** a one-page report a manager understands in five seconds**Time** 11 hours**You finish with** the Kettle & Crumb sales dashboard
A good dashboard answers one question for one person. Decide the question first, then choose visuals. Design is mostly removing things: fewer colours, fewer charts, fewer decimals.
A layout that works for most one-page reports
Eyes start top-left. Put the headline numbers there (1), then what changed over time (2), then what explains it (3), then the rows for people who want proof (4). Slicers sit together in one place.

Card, or the new card visual with a reference label

blocks.text: **One accent colour**Grey for context, one colour for the thing to notice. Red and green only for bad and good.
**Titles that say something**"Sales fell in February" beats "Sales by Month".
**Slicers and interactions**Slicers filter the page. Edit interactions decides which visuals react to a click.
**Drill-through and tooltips**Keep the first page simple. Send detail to a drill-through page or a report page tooltip.
**Bookmarks**Save a state of the page. Used for view toggles and guided stories.
**Accessibility**Enough contrast, alt text on visuals, a sensible tab order, and never colour as the only signal.

modules.title: Week 5: Advanced Power Query, built to scale

lessons.title: Week 5: Advanced Power Query, built to scale

blocks.text: **Goal** queries that handle many files and large tables**Time** 10 hours**You finish with** a folder-driven Orders query with a parameter and a reusable function

Week 1 cleaned one file by hand. Real work has a new file every month and tables with millions of rows. This week you make the same cleaning steps reusable, and you learn why some queries refresh in seconds while others take an hour.
**Parameter**A named value, such as a folder path or a region, that queries read. Change it once and every query follows.*Home, Manage Parameters.*
**Custom function**A query that takes an input and returns a result. Write a cleaning rule once and call it on any column or file.
**Combine files from a folder**Point at a folder. Power BI builds the steps on one sample file and runs them on every file, then stacks the results.
**Query folding**With a database source, Power Query turns your steps into one SQL query so the database does the work. A step it cannot translate runs on your PC, and so does everything after it.
**try ... otherwise**Catches a conversion error in one cell and returns a fallback, so one bad value does not fail the whole refresh.
**Incremental refresh**Reload only recent rows, such as the last 7 days, and keep older data as it is. Needs two date/time parameters named exactly `RangeStart` and `RangeEnd`.
How a folder of files becomes one table

Get data, Folder, then Combine & Transform Data. Power BI creates the two highlighted pieces for you. Edit the sample file's steps and every file gets the same treatment. A new file dropped in the folder is picked up at the next refresh.
Where does each step run? (illustrative numbers)

The source is a database table. A merge with an Excel file cannot be turned into SQL, because the database cannot see the Excel file. Put that step late, after the filters and grouping, and the database still does the heavy work. Which steps fold depends on the connector, so right-click a step and look for View Native Query, or read the folding indicator next to each step.
Pattern 4 uses `>=` on one side and `<` on the other so a row on the boundary is never loaded twice.

Mistakes people make this week

items: Hard-coding a path like C:\Users\you\Desktop in the query. Nobody else can refresh it. Use a parameter.
Putting a non-folding step first on a large database table, so every row is downloaded.
Using Replace Errors on a whole table without reading the errors. It hides real data problems.

blocks.text: Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: A query on a database table of 2 million rows takes 20 minutes to refresh. The second step is a merge with an Excel file, and the filters come after it. What do you change?
options: Add Table.Buffer after the source
Move the filter and remove-column steps before the merge so they fold into SQL, then confirm with View Native Query
Switch off background refresh
Split the query into ten queries
quiz.why: Once a step cannot be translated to SQL, every later step runs on your PC against all the rows. Filtering first lets the database return a small result. Try both positions in the simulator.

quiz.q: A new monthly CSV with the same columns lands in one folder every month. How should the Orders query be built?
options: One query per file, appended by hand each month
Get data from Folder, then Combine & Transform, with the cleaning steps in the sample file query
Paste each month into one large Excel sheet
A calculated table in DAX using UNION
quiz.why: The folder connector builds a function from the sample file and runs it on every file. A new file is included at the next refresh with no edits.

quiz.q: A few amount cells contain N/A, so the type change shows errors and the refresh fails. You want real numbers kept and the bad cells empty. What is the cleanest fix?
options: Remove every row that has an error
Leave the column as text
Convert with try Number.FromText([amount]) otherwise null
Replace N/A with 0
quiz.why: try ... otherwise catches the error per cell and returns null, which means unknown. Removing rows loses orders, text cannot be summed, and 0 would pull averages down.

blocks.text: **Goal** handle two dates, many-to-many, big data and security**Time** 11 hours**You finish with** a model with a delivery date, three security roles and a clear storage choice

A star schema covers most reports. Four situations need more: a fact with two dates, two things that relate many-to-many, data too large or too fresh to copy, and people who must see only their own rows.

**Role-playing dimension**One Date table used for two purposes, such as order date and delivery date. Only one relationship can be active. The other is switched on inside a measure with USERELATIONSHIP.
**Bridge table**A small table that sits between two tables that relate many-to-many, with one row per valid pair.*A product can be in many promotions. A promotion covers many products.*
**Storage mode**Import copies data into the model. DirectQuery leaves it in the source and asks on every click. Dual does either, as needed. Direct Lake reads Fabric lake files directly.
**Composite model**A model that mixes modes, such as an imported Products table with a DirectQuery fact.
**Row-level security**A DAX filter attached to a role. A member of the role sees only the rows where the filter is true, in every visual and every total.*Modeling, Manage roles.*
**Dynamic security**One role for everyone. The filter compares a column with the signed-in user: `Stores[manager_email] = USERPRINCIPALNAME()`.
One Date table, two dates
Total Sales by order month against Delivered Sales by delivery month

blocks.code:
Delivered Sales =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales],
        USERELATIONSHIP ( Orders[delivery date], 'Date'[Date] ) )

blocks.text: Computed on the 20 practice orders with delivery set to two days after the order. Both columns add to the same total. Orders placed in the last days of a month move into the next month, which is why February and March differ.
Many-to-many through a bridge

A promotion filter has to travel right, through the bridge, into Products and on to Orders. The middle link normally filters from Products to the bridge only. Either set that one relationship to Both, or keep it single and write `CALCULATE([Total Sales], CROSSFILTER(PromoProducts[product], Products[product], BOTH))`.

With Import the source is touched only at refresh, so visuals are fast and the data is as old as the last refresh. With DirectQuery the arrows point the other way: nothing is stored, and each visual waits for the source to answer.

rows: Delta files in a Fabric lakehouse

blocks.text: Mini-project: two dates and three roles

items: Loading a second copy of the Date table for every date column when one inactive relationship would do. A second Date table is fine when readers need to slice by both dates at once.
Choosing DirectQuery because it sounds modern. It moves the performance problem to the database.
Building security with hidden pages or slicers. Anyone can undo those. Only roles are security.

blocks.text: A documented limit: Microsoft's reference says USERELATIONSHIP can raise an error when row-level security is defined on the tables in that relationship. In this project the roles filter Stores, and the inactive relationship joins Orders and Date. If you do hit the error in your own model, give the second date its own Date table instead.
Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: Orders has an order date and a delivery date. Most measures use order date. One measure must total sales by delivery month. What do you build?
options: A second copy of Orders related on delivery date
An inactive relationship from Date to Orders[delivery date], used with USERELATIONSHIP inside CALCULATE
Both relationships set to active
A text column holding the delivery month
quiz.why: Two tables can have only one active relationship. The inactive one waits until a measure asks for it with USERELATIONSHIP.

quiz.q: Three regional managers open the same report. Each must see only their own region, including in totals and exports. What is the right design?
options: Three copies of the report
A region slicer locked on each page
Hide the other regions' pages
Row-level security roles filtering Stores[region], with each manager assigned as a Viewer
quiz.why: Only a role is enforced by the model. Slicers and hidden pages can be undone, and copies triple the maintenance. Roles apply to people with the Viewer role.

quiz.q: A warehouse table has 500 million rows and the report must show orders from the last minute. Which storage mode fits the fact table?
options: Import with a refresh every hour
DirectQuery, accepting that visuals wait for the source
A CSV export loaded with Import
Import with Auto date/time switched on
quiz.why: The data is too large to copy comfortably and too fresh for a schedule. DirectQuery asks the source on each interaction. Keep small dimensions in Dual or Import so slicers stay quick.

modules.title: Week 7: Advanced DAX, thinking in tables

lessons.title: Week 7: Advanced DAX, thinking in tables

blocks.text: **Goal** rank, accumulate and compare against any total**Time** 12 hours**You finish with** ranking, running totals, share measures and a calculation group

Week 3 measures returned one number from the current filters. Advanced DAX builds a small table in memory first, such as one row per product, and then works on that table. Three ideas carry most of it: context transition, the ALL family, and iterating over a list of values.

blocks.code:
Wrong = SUMX ( Products, SUM ( Orders[qty] ) )
Right = SUMX ( Products, CALCULATE ( SUM ( Orders[qty] ) ) )

blocks.text: Being on a row does not filter anything. CALCULATE turns the current row into a filter. Every measure has a hidden CALCULATE around it, which is why calling `[Total Sales]` inside SUMX works per row.
**ALL and REMOVEFILTERS**Ignore filters on a column or table. The denominator becomes the grand total.
**ALLSELECTED**Ignore the filter from the visual's own rows, but keep slicers. The denominator becomes the visible total.
**ALLEXCEPT**Remove every filter on a table except the columns you name. Used for a share within a group.
**VALUES**The distinct values of a column that are visible right now. Iterate over it to work per customer, per month or per product.
**RANKX and TOPN**RANKX gives a position. TOPN returns the best rows as a table you can filter by.
**Calculation group**A calculation such as YTD written once with `SELECTEDMEASURE()` and applied to any measure.*Model view, Calculation group.*

lessons.title: Share of what? ALL against ALLSELECTED

blocks.text: Category share with a region slicer

blocks.code:
% of All      = DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS () ) )
% of Selected = DIVIDE ( [Total Sales],
                    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Products[category] ) ) )

blocks.text: With no slicer the two columns match. Pick a region and they separate: % of All divides by every sale in the model, while % of Selected divides by what the slicer leaves, so it always adds to 100.
What these measures return on the practice data

blocks.code:
Product Rank =
    IF ( HASONEVALUE ( Products[product] ),
        RANKX ( ALL ( Products[product] ), [Total Sales] ) )

Cumulative % =
    VAR Cur = [Total Sales]
    VAR Bigger = FILTER ( ALL ( Products[product] ), [Total Sales] >= Cur )
    RETURN DIVIDE ( SUMX ( Bigger, [Total Sales] ),
                    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALL ( Products[product] ) ) )

Running Total =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales],
        FILTER ( ALL ( 'Date'[Date] ), 'Date'[Date] <= MAX ( 'Date'[Date] ) ) )

Avg Sales per Customer = AVERAGEX ( VALUES ( Orders[customer] ), [Total Sales] )

Top 3 Sales =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], TOPN ( 3, ALL ( Products[product] ), [Total Sales] ) )

blocks.text: Each measure removes the filter from the row it is on, builds the full list, then compares the current row against it. Rank counts how many products sell more. Cumulative % adds every product that sells at least as much. One documented catch: when products tie at the cut-off, TOPN returns all of the tied rows, so Top 3 can cover four products.

blocks.code:
// Calculation group "Time view", three calculation items
Current = SELECTEDMEASURE ()
YTD     = CALCULATE ( SELECTEDMEASURE (), DATESYTD ( 'Date'[Date] ) )
vs PM % =
    VAR Prev = CALCULATE ( SELECTEDMEASURE (), DATEADD ( 'Date'[Date], -1, MONTH ) )
    RETURN DIVIDE ( SELECTEDMEASURE () - Prev, Prev )

blocks.text: Put the Time view column on a matrix's columns and any measure in values. Total Sales, Profit and Orders Count all get Current, YTD and vs PM % without nine separate measures. Power BI asks you to switch on "discourage implicit measures" first, because calculation items only apply to measures you wrote.
Making DAX fast

items: Store a value in a `VAR` when you use it twice. It is calculated once.
Filter a column, not a whole table: `Products[category] = "Tea"` beats `FILTER ( Products, ... )`.
Find the slow visual with View, Performance analyzer, then copy its query into DAX query view to test changes.
Fix the model before the measure. A missing relationship or a wide flat table costs more than any formula.

blocks.text: Mini-project: the analyst's page
Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: SUMX ( Products, SUM ( Orders[qty] ) ) returns 252 on the practice data, but the total quantity is 42. Why?
options: SUMX does not work on dimension tables
There is no context transition, so SUM returns all 42 for each of the 6 products
The relationship is inactive
qty is stored as text
quiz.why: A row context does not filter. Without CALCULATE, or a measure, the inner SUM sees every order each time: 42 × 6 = 252.

quiz.q: A slicer has North and South selected. A table lists categories. You want each category's share of what is visible, adding to 100%. Which denominator?
options: CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS () )
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Products[category] ) )
SUM ( Orders[amount] )
[Total Sales]
quiz.why: ALLSELECTED removes the filter from the table's own rows and keeps the slicer, so the base is the visible total. REMOVEFILTERS () would divide by all three regions.

quiz.q: You want a rank column where the best-selling product shows 1. Which measure is right?
options: RANKX ( Products, [Total Sales] )
RANKX ( ALL ( Products[product] ), [Total Sales] )
TOPN ( 1, Products, [Total Sales] )
A calculated column sorting Products[price]
quiz.why: On each row the visual has already filtered Products to one product, so ranking within Products always gives 1. ALL restores the full list to rank against.

blocks.text: **Goal** a report other people can rely on**Time** 11 hours**You finish with** a published report with scheduled refresh, tested security and a safe way to change it

A report on your laptop helps nobody. This week moves it to the Power BI service, keeps its data fresh, controls who sees what, and sets up a way to change it without breaking what people use every morning. You need a work or school account for this week.
From your PC to the reader

Publishing sends two things to the workspace: the semantic model and the report. Readers get the app, not the workspace. The service can reach cloud sources by itself. For anything on your network or your own disk it needs a gateway to fetch the data.
**Workspace**A shared folder in the service for the people who build. Roles: Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer.
**App**A packaged, read-only view of a workspace for the people who read. One link, clean navigation.
**Scheduled refresh**The service reloads the data on a timetable using saved credentials, and emails you when it fails.
**Security in the service**Open the semantic model's menu, choose Security, add people to roles, then Test as role. Roles apply to Viewers only. Admins, Members and Contributors see everything.
**Deployment pipeline**Development, Test and Production stages, each its own workspace. You change Development and promote when it is right.
**Power BI project**File, Save as, Power BI project. The report and model become text files you can keep in Git and compare line by line.
Do I need a gateway?
Pick where the data lives
Most first-time refresh failures are this question. The service runs in the cloud and cannot see your C: drive.

Mistakes people make this week

items: Giving readers the Member role so they can open the report. They can now edit it, and security roles no longer apply to them.
Editing the live report directly. Keep a development copy.

blocks.text: Quiz: 3 practical questions

quiz.q: Your published report reads an Excel file from C:\Reports on your laptop. Scheduled refresh fails every night. What is the fix?
options: Refresh more often
Install a data gateway on that PC, or move the file to OneDrive or SharePoint and connect to it there
Republish the report each morning
Switch the table to DirectQuery
quiz.why: The service cannot reach a local disk. A gateway fetches the file for it, and it only works while that PC is on. A cloud location removes the need.

quiz.q: You created security roles in Desktop and published. A colleague still sees every region. What is the most likely cause?
options: Roles only work in Desktop
Nobody was added to the roles in the service, or the colleague has an edit role in the workspace
The Date table is not marked
The report needs a region slicer
quiz.why: Members are assigned in the service under the semantic model's Security page. Roles apply to Viewers only, so an Admin, Member or Contributor sees everything.

quiz.q: Managers use the sales report every morning. You need to rebuild two measures and a page. How do you do it safely?
options: Edit the live report in the browser
Work in a development workspace, check it in test, then promote to production
Publish over the live report and fix problems as they are reported
Email a .pbix file to each manager
quiz.why: A deployment pipeline, or at least a separate development workspace, lets you change and test without touching what people rely on.

items: **Portfolio:** three reports on public data you care about, each with a short note on the question, the model and one insight.
**Certification:** Microsoft's PL-300 exam covers preparing data, modeling, visualising and managing reports, which is the ground of these eight weeks.
**Habit:** rebuild one dashboard you admire each month. Copying a layout teaches more than reading about one.

blocks.text: How this page was checked

items: Every number on the page is calculated by the page from the 20 practice orders, so the check totals cannot drift from the data.

Function syntax and menu paths were read against Microsoft Learn in November 2026: 20 functions and features across DAX, Power Query and the service, including RANKX, TOPN, ALLSELECTED, CROSSFILTER, DATEADD, USERELATIONSHIP and REMOVEFILTERS.
The DAX and M were not executed in Power BI Desktop, which needs Windows. If a formula errors for you, the Q&A bank has a debugging entry, and menu names can shift between monthly releases.

questions.q: What is the difference between Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service?
questions.a: Desktop is the free Windows app where you build: Power Query, the model, DAX and report pages. The service is the website where you publish, share, schedule refresh and build dashboards from pinned visuals.

questions.q: What is the difference between a report and a dashboard?
questions.a: A report is one or more pages of visuals built on one semantic model, with slicers and interactions. A dashboard, in the service, is a single canvas of tiles pinned from reports. In everyday speech people call a one-page report a dashboard.

questions.q: Do I need to know SQL or Excel first?
questions.a: No. Excel habits help with formulas and SQL helps with joins, but Power Query is point-and-click and DAX is learned on its own terms.

questions.q: What licence do I need?
questions.a: Building in Desktop is free. Sharing reports with other people in the service normally needs a paid licence or capacity. Check Microsoft's current licensing page, because the plans change.

questions.q: Does Power Query change my source file?
questions.a: Never. It reads the source and applies steps to a copy in memory. The original Excel or CSV file is untouched.

questions.q: What is the difference between Merge and Append?
questions.a: Merge joins two tables side by side on a matching key and brings in columns. Append stacks tables on top of each other and adds rows.

questions.q: What is the difference between Duplicate and Reference?
questions.a: Duplicate copies all the steps into an independent query. Reference starts a new query from the output of the first, so a fix in the original flows through.

questions.q: Why are there errors in my column after changing the type?
questions.a: Some values cannot convert, such as text in a number column or a day-first date read as month-first. Click the cell's error to see why, fix the cause with Replace Values or Using Locale, and avoid blanket Replace Errors.

questions.q: What is M?
questions.a: The language Power Query writes for you behind each step. You can read and edit it in the formula bar or Advanced Editor. You rarely need to write it from scratch as a beginner.

questions.q: What is query folding?
questions.a: When the source is a database, Power Query translates your steps into one SQL query so the database does the work. Filter and remove columns early to keep folding going.

questions.q: Should I clean data in Power Query or with DAX?
questions.a: Clean and shape in Power Query. Calculate in DAX. If a value never changes with slicers and can be made at load, make it upstream.

questions.q: When should I unpivot?
questions.a: When column headers are really values, such as months, years or product names across the top. After unpivoting, they sit in one column you can filter and chart.

questions.q: What is a star schema?
questions.a: One fact table of events surrounded by dimension tables that describe them, linked by one-to-many relationships. It is the shape Power BI is designed around.

questions.q: How do I tell a fact table from a dimension?
questions.a: Facts answer how many or how much and grow every day. Dimensions answer who, what, where and when and change slowly.

questions.q: Why do I need a separate Date table?
questions.a: To get every day in a continuous range, to add fiscal years or weekdays once for all facts, to sort month names properly, and because time intelligence functions rely on it.

questions.q: Should I use both-direction cross filtering?
questions.a: Rarely. It can create ambiguous filter paths and slow the model. Keep single direction and solve special cases in a measure.

questions.q: What is cardinality?
questions.a: How rows match across a relationship: one-to-many is normal, one-to-one usually means the tables could be merged, many-to-many needs care or a bridge table.

questions.q: Why does a relationship show a dotted line?
questions.a: It is inactive. Only one active path can exist between two tables. Use USERELATIONSHIP inside CALCULATE to use the inactive one in a specific measure.

questions.q: My month names sort alphabetically. How do I fix it?
questions.a: Select the Month column in the Date table, choose Sort by column, and pick the Month No column.

questions.q: Should I turn off Auto date/time?
questions.a: Yes, once you have your own Date table. It creates a hidden date table for every date column, which bloats the file. The setting is under Options, Data Load.

questions.q: What is the difference between a measure and a calculated column?
questions.a: A column is computed per row at refresh and stored. A measure is computed at query time under the current filters. Use measures for numbers in visuals and columns for things you group or slice by.

questions.q: What is filter context?
questions.a: The set of filters active for one cell of a visual: slicers, the row and column headers, page filters and cross-highlighting. A measure is evaluated on the rows those filters leave.

questions.q: What is row context?
questions.a: Being positioned on one row of a table while a formula runs, as in a calculated column or inside SUMX. Row context does not filter other tables by itself.

questions.q: What does CALCULATE do?
questions.a: It evaluates an expression after changing the filter context. Its filter arguments add, replace or remove filters. It also turns a row context into a filter context, which is called context transition.

questions.q: What is the difference between SUM and SUMX?
questions.a: SUM adds one column. SUMX goes row by row through a table, evaluates an expression for each row, then adds the results. Use SUMX when you need to multiply or combine columns first.

questions.q: What is the difference between ALL and REMOVEFILTERS?
questions.a: As a filter argument in CALCULATE they do the same thing: clear filters. REMOVEFILTERS states the intent more clearly. ALL can also be used as a table function that returns all rows.

questions.q: Why use DIVIDE and not the slash?
questions.a: DIVIDE returns blank, or a value you choose, when the bottom is zero or blank. The slash returns an error or infinity.

questions.q: Why is my total row not the sum of the rows above?
questions.a: The total is not added up. The measure is evaluated again with no row filter. For ratios and distinct counts this is correct. If you truly need a sum of visible rows, iterate with SUMX over the grouping column.

questions.q: How do I debug a measure?
questions.a: Split it into variables and return one variable at a time. Put the measure in a table with the dimension you care about. For deeper checks, use DAX query view to run the expression directly.

questions.q: When do I need RELATED?
questions.a: Inside a row context on the many side when you need a value from the one side, such as the product price while iterating Orders.

questions.q: How many visuals should a page have?
questions.a: As few as answer the question. Five to eight is a comfortable upper range for one page. If you scroll or squint, split the page.

questions.q: When is a pie chart acceptable?
questions.a: For two or three parts of one whole, where one part is clearly bigger. For anything else a sorted bar chart is easier to read.

questions.q: How do I choose colours?
questions.a: Start with grey for most marks and one accent for emphasis. Keep the same colour for the same category on every page. Use red and green only for status, and pair them with an icon or label for colour-blind readers.

questions.q: What is the difference between a slicer and a filter?
questions.a: A slicer is on the canvas and visible to readers. Filters live in the Filters pane and can apply to one visual, a page, or all pages. Use slicers for choices readers make often.

questions.q: What is drill-through?
questions.a: A right-click jump from a data point to a detail page that is filtered to that item, such as from a product bar to a product page.

questions.q: How do I make a report fast?
questions.a: Fewer visuals per page, a star schema, measures in place of heavy calculated columns, no unneeded columns in the model, and a check with Performance analyzer to find the slow visual.

questions.q: What is row-level security?
questions.a: Roles with DAX filters on tables, so each user sees only permitted rows. You define roles in Desktop and assign people to them in the service.

questions.q: What is the difference between Import and DirectQuery?
questions.a: Import stores a compressed copy in the model and is fast but needs refresh. DirectQuery sends queries to the source on every interaction, so data is current but speed depends on the source.

questions.q: What is incremental refresh?
questions.a: A policy that refreshes only recent data, such as the last 7 days, and keeps older partitions as they are. It makes large tables practical.

questions.q: What are calculation groups?
questions.a: A way to define a calculation such as YTD or previous year once and apply it to any measure, which avoids writing dozens of near-identical measures.

questions.q: What is a Power Query parameter used for?
questions.a: A named value that queries read, such as a folder path, a server name or a cut-off date. You change it in one place, and it can differ between development and production.

questions.q: When should I write a custom function in Power Query?
questions.a: When the same cleaning logic is needed on several columns, files or queries. Combine files from a folder creates one for you from the sample file.

questions.q: How do I know whether a step folds?
questions.a: Right-click the step. If View Native Query is available, the step folds and you can read the SQL. Recent versions also show a folding indicator beside each step. Folding depends on the connector.

questions.q: What is context transition?
questions.a: Inside a row-by-row loop, CALCULATE turns the current row into filters. Measures carry an implicit CALCULATE, so a measure called inside SUMX is evaluated for that row only.

questions.q: What is the difference between ALL and ALLSELECTED?
questions.a: ALL ignores every filter on the column or table, so you get the grand total. ALLSELECTED ignores only the filter from the visual's own rows and columns and keeps slicers, so you get the visible total.

questions.q: When do I need a bridge table?
questions.a: When two tables relate many-to-many, such as products and promotions, or customers and accounts. The bridge holds one row per valid pair and sits between them.

questions.q: What is dynamic row-level security?
questions.a: One role whose filter compares a column with the signed-in user, for example Stores[manager_email] = USERPRINCIPALNAME(). Access is then managed by editing a mapping table, not by creating roles.

questions.q: Does row-level security apply to everyone?
questions.a: No. It applies to people with the Viewer role. Workspace Admins, Members and Contributors can edit the model, so they see all rows.

questions.q: What is a composite model?
questions.a: A model that mixes storage modes, such as imported dimensions with a DirectQuery fact table, or your own tables added on top of a shared semantic model.

questions.q: What is Direct Lake?
questions.a: A storage mode in Microsoft Fabric where the model reads Delta files in a lakehouse directly. It aims for Import-like speed without a separate copy and refresh.

questions.q: When do I need a data gateway?
questions.a: When the service must refresh from something it cannot reach from the cloud: a file on a PC, a network share, or a database on your company network. Cloud sources usually do not need one.

questions.q: What is the difference between a workspace and an app?
questions.a: A workspace is where builders keep and edit content. An app is a read-only package published from a workspace for readers, with its own navigation and audience.

questions.q: What is a deployment pipeline?
questions.a: A set of stages, by default Development, Test and Production, each tied to a workspace. You promote content from one stage to the next when it is ready.

questions.q: What is a .pbip file?
questions.a: A Power BI project. The report and semantic model are saved as folders of text files, which makes them suitable for Git, code review and comparing versions.

questions.q: What is a field parameter?
questions.a: A parameter that lets readers choose which measure or which column a visual uses, through a slicer. Created from Modeling, New parameter, Fields.

questions.q: How do I find out why a report page is slow?
questions.a: Open View, Performance analyzer, start recording and refresh the visuals. It shows the time each visual spends on the DAX query and on drawing. Copy the slow query into DAX query view to test changes.
